question.text: An investor compares three gold investment options: Physical Gold, Gold ETF, and Sovereign Gold Bond held to maturity. Assuming identical gold price appreciation and ignoring transaction costs, which option provides the HIGHEST post-tax return?

answer.text: Physical Gold, because there is no expense ratio
Gold ETF, because it tracks gold prices most accurately
Sovereign Gold Bond, because of 2.50% annual interest and tax-free capital gains at maturity
All three provide identical post-tax returns since gold appreciation is the same

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook gives SGBs two tax advantages other gold products do not have: they pay 2.50% interest, and the redemption with RBI table shows no tax on redemption. Physical gold and Gold ETFs have no interest income and gains are taxable as capital gains, so SGBs held to maturity deliver the highest post-tax return. The Trap: Physical gold still bears storage, insurance, purity and making-charge costs; Gold ETF tracking accuracy does not change its tax treatment; and the identical-returns option ignores both the SGB interest and the redemption exemption. Note: Based on NISM Series X-B workbook pp.265-266 and 426, which set out the SGB interest, RBI redemption treatment, and tax treatment of other gold products.
